==Problem==

Let <math>p</math>, <math>q</math>, and <math>r</math> be the distinct roots of the polynomial <math>x^3 - 22x^2 + 80x - 67</math>. It is given that there exist real numbers <math>A</math>, <math>B</math>, and <math>C</math> such that <cmath>\dfrac{1}{s^3 - 22s^2 + 80s - 67} = \dfrac{A}{s-p} + \dfrac{B}{s-q} + \frac{C}{s-r}</cmath>for all <math>s\not\in\{p,q,r\}</math>. What is <math>\tfrac1A+\tfrac1B+\tfrac1C</math>?

<math>\textbf{(A) }243\qquad\textbf{(B) }244\qquad\textbf{(C) }245\qquad\textbf{(D) }246\qquad\textbf{(E) } 247</math>

==Solution 1==
Multiplying both sides by <imath>(s-p)(s-q)(s-r)</imath> yields
<cmath>1 = A(s-q)(s-r) + B(s-p)(s-r) + C(s-p)(s-q)</cmath>
As this is a polynomial identity, and it is true for infinitely many <imath>s</imath>, it must be true for all <imath>s</imath> (since a polynomial with infinitely many roots must in fact be the constant polynomial <imath>0</imath>). This means we can plug in <imath>s = p</imath> to find that <imath>\frac1A = (p-q)(p-r)</imath>.  Similarly, we can find <imath>\frac1B = (q-p)(q-r)</imath> and <imath>\frac1C = (r-p)(r-q)</imath>.  Summing them up, we get that <cmath>\frac1A + \frac1B + \frac1C = p^2 + q^2 + r^2 - pq - qr - pr</cmath>
We can express <imath>p^2 + q^2 + r^2 = (p+q+r)^2 - 3(pq + qr + pr)</imath>, and by Vieta's Formulas, we know that this expression is equal to <imath>484</imath>. Vieta's also gives <imath>pq + qr + pr = 80</imath> (which we also used to find <imath>p^2+q^2+r^2</imath>), so the answer is <imath>484 -240 = \boxed{\textbf{(B) } 244}</imath>. 

''Note'': this process of substituting in the 'forbidden' values in the original identity is a standard technique for partial fraction decomposition, as taught in calculus classes.

==Solution 2 (Pure Elementary Algebra)==
Solution 1 uses a trick from Calculus that seemingly contradicts the restriction <imath>s\not\in\{p,q,r\}</imath>. Here is a solution with pure elementary algebra.
<cmath>A(s-q)(s-r) + B(s-p)(s-r) + C(s-p)(s-q)=1</cmath>
<cmath>s^2(A+B+C)-s(Aq+Ar+Bp+Br+Cp+Cq)+(Aqr+Bpr+Cpq-1)=0</cmath>
<cmath>\begin{cases}
A+B+C=0 & (1)\\
Aq+Ar+Bp+Br+Cp+Cq=0 & (2)\\
Aqr+Bpr+Cpq=1 & (3)
\end{cases}</cmath>
From <imath>(1)</imath> we get <imath>A=-(B+C)</imath>, <imath>B=-(A+C)</imath>, <imath>C=-(A+B)</imath>, substituting them in <imath>(2)</imath>, we get <imath>Ap + Bq + Cr=0</imath>  <imath>(4)</imath>

<imath>(4)- (1) \cdot r</imath>, <imath>A(p-r)+B(q-r)=0</imath>  <imath>(5)</imath>

<imath>(3) - (1) \cdot pq</imath>, <imath>Aq(r-p)+Bp(r-q)=1</imath>  <imath>(6)</imath>

<imath>(6) + (5) \cdot p</imath>, <imath>A(r-p)(q-p)=1</imath>

<imath>A = \frac{1}{(r-p)(q-p)}</imath>, by symmetry, <imath>B = \frac{1}{(r-q)(p-q)}</imath>, <imath>C = \frac{1}{(q-r)(p-r)}</imath>

The rest is similar to solution 1, we get <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 244}</imath>
